title: Force & Momentum — Chapter Test
sourceKeysNote: Keys audited and corrected for testing; source has 5-option Q24, conflicting keys for Q2/Q14/Q19/Q38/Q39, and ambiguous wording for Q21/Q27/Q42/Q45; corrected render and grading explicitly documented.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Momentum may be expressed in:
questions.explanation: Momentum has units kg·m/s, equivalent to newton-second (N·s).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The momentum of an object at a given instant is independent of its:
questions.explanation: Momentum p = mv depends on mass and velocity, not acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two bodies A and B have equal kinetic energies. The mass of A is nine times that of B. The ratio of the momentum of A to B is:
questions.explanation: At equal kinetic energy, p = √(2mK), so pA/pB = √9 = 3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two objects P and Q have the same momentum. Q has more kinetic energy than P if Q:
questions.explanation: For equal momentum, K = p²/(2m); the lighter, faster body has greater kinetic energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 1.0-kg ball moving at 2.0 m/s perpendicular to a wall rebounds at 1.5 m/s. The change in momentum is:
questions.explanation: Taking away from the wall as positive, Δp = 1(1.5 − (−2.0)) = 3.5 N·s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the total momentum of a system is changing:
options: particles must exert forces on each other
the system must be under gravity
the center of mass must have constant velocity
a net external force must act on the system
questions.explanation: The rate of change of total momentum equals the net external force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When a driver accelerates a car, the force that accelerates the car is:
options: the force of the foot on the accelerator
the static friction of the road on the tires
the force of the engine on the drive shaft
the normal force of the road on the tires
questions.explanation: The road exerts forward static friction on the driven tires.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 2.5-kg stone is released from rest. After falling for 4.0 s, the magnitude of its momentum is approximately:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A projectile explodes into fragments in flight. Immediately after the explosion, their total momentum:
options: equals the projectile's momentum immediately before explosion
has changed into fragment kinetic energy
is smaller than its original value
is greater than its original value
questions.explanation: The explosion is internal; external impulse during the brief event is negligible.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A rifle of mass M at rest fires a bullet of mass m at ground-frame velocity v. The rifle's recoil velocity is:
questions.explanation: Initial momentum is zero, so MV + mv = 0 and V = −mv/M.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The thrust of a rocket is:
options: a gravitational force on the rocket
the force of expelled fuel gases on the rocket
any force external to the rocket-fuel system
only the loss of rocket mass
questions.explanation: Expelled gases exert the opposite reaction force on the rocket.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Impulse has the same dimensions as:
questions.explanation: Impulse FΔt equals the change in momentum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Conservation of momentum applies to colliding bodies when:
options: the coefficient of restitution equals one
the coefficient of restitution equals zero
the net external impulse is zero
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved if the system has zero net external impulse.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two spheres collide head-on. The magnitude of the impulse of sphere X on sphere Y is:
options: twice the impulse of Y on X
half the impulse of Y on X
one-fourth the impulse of Y on X
the same as the impulse of Y on X
questions.explanation: Newton's third law gives equal and opposite contact forces and impulses.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An airbag stops a passenger's head over more time than a windshield. Compared with the windshield, the airbag:
options: causes a much smaller momentum change
causes a much smaller kinetic-energy change
exerts a much smaller average force
questions.explanation: For the same momentum change, increasing collision time reduces average force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An inelastic collision is one in which:
options: momentum is not conserved but kinetic energy is
total mass is not conserved but momentum is
neither momentum nor kinetic energy is conserved
momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not
questions.explanation: In an isolated inelastic collision, momentum is conserved but kinetic energy decreases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 4.0-N puck moves at 3.0 m/s and hits a stationary 8.0-N puck. They stick together. Their common final speed is:
questions.explanation: Momentum conservation gives v = (4×3)/(4+8) = 1 m/s; weights are proportional to masses.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 3.00-g bullet at 400 m/s embeds in a 3.00-kg block at rest. The final speed of the block-bullet system is approximately:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 3-g bullet embeds in a suspended 10-kg block. The block rises 3 mm. The bullet's initial speed is approximately:
questions.explanation: After impact v = √(2gh) ≈ 0.243 m/s. Momentum gives bullet speed ≈ (10.003/0.003)×0.243 ≈ 810 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An elastic collision is one in which:
options: total mass is not conserved but momentum is
both kinetic energy and momentum are conserved
momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not
questions.explanation: In an isolated elastic collision both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 2.0-kg block A moving at +5.0 m/s undergoes a one-dimensional elastic collision with stationary block B. If B is much more massive, A's velocity afterward is approximately:
questions.explanation: A light body striking a much heavier stationary body elastically rebounds at about its initial speed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A very massive body at 10 m/s elastically strikes a very light stationary body. The lighter body's final speed is approximately:
questions.explanation: For M ≫ m, the light body's speed approaches 2u = 20 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Sphere A (mass m, speed v) makes a head-on elastic collision with stationary sphere B (mass 2m). Their final velocities (vA, vB) are:
questions.explanation: One-dimensional elastic collision formulas give vA = −v/3 and vB = 2v/3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a head-on elastic collision with an initially stationary target, the greatest fraction of kinetic energy is transferred when:
options: the two colliding particles have equal mass
the incident particle is initially moving very slowly
the incident particle is much more massive
the incident particle is much less massive
questions.explanation: Energy transfer fraction 4mM/(m+M)² is greatest at m = M. Original source had five choices, so its correct E was moved to A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Momentum may be described by: I. quantity of motion; II. difficulty of stopping a moving body; III. mass × velocity; IV. moment × force. Which are valid?
questions.explanation: Momentum is mass times velocity and measures how difficult moving matter is to stop.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What force changes the speed of a 2-kg body from 20 m/s to 30 m/s in 2 seconds?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body of mass M strikes a smooth wall elastically at 60° to the wall's normal, with speed V. The magnitude of momentum change is:
questions.explanation: Normal momentum reverses; |Δp| = 2MV cos60° = MV. Angle reference made explicit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A light and a heavy body have the same momentum. Which has more kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: K = p²/(2m), so smaller mass means greater kinetic energy for the same p.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If a body's momentum becomes n times its original value, its kinetic energy becomes:
questions.explanation: For constant mass, K = p²/(2m), so K scales as n².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A sphere of mass m and speed V embeds in a hanging sandbag of mass M, and the combination rises height h. The initial speed V is:
questions.explanation: After collision, speed is √(2gh); momentum gives mV = (M+m)√(2gh).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A rifle recoils freely after firing a bullet. Its recoil kinetic energy is:
options: less than that of the bullet
more than that of the bullet
the same as that of the bullet
equal to or less than that of the bullet
questions.explanation: The bullet and rifle have equal momentum magnitude; K = p²/(2m) is smaller for the heavier rifle.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 12-kg bomb splits into parts with mass ratio 1:3. The smaller part has kinetic energy 216 J. The magnitude of momentum of the larger part is:
questions.explanation: Smaller mass is 3 kg. p = √(2×3×216) = 36 kg·m/s; both fragments have equal opposite momenta.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The kinetic energy of a 2-kg body with momentum 2 N·s is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which particle has the greatest kinetic energy for the same momentum?
questions.explanation: K = p²/(2m), and the electron has the smallest mass.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object of mass 3m splits into three equal parts. Two travel at velocities vĵ and vî. The third fragment's velocity is:
questions.explanation: Zero initial momentum requires the third velocity to be the negative vector sum of the other two.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Momentum conservation can be applied during a collision between particles when the impact duration is:
options: dependent on the type of collision
questions.explanation: The shorter the impact, the less external impulse influences the collision system.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A lead ball strikes a wall and falls. A tennis ball of equal mass and incoming speed rebounds. Which is true?
options: the lead ball has greater initial momentum
the lead ball has greater momentum change
the tennis ball has greater momentum change
questions.explanation: Reversing velocity yields a larger Δp magnitude than merely stopping.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A stationary ²³⁸U nucleus emits an alpha particle of mass 4u with velocity +v. The recoil velocity of the residual nucleus (mass 234u) is:
questions.explanation: Conservation of momentum gives 234u·V + 4u·v = 0, hence V = −4v/234.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A moving shell of mass m and velocity v splits into two pieces. The piece of mass m/4 stops. The other piece's speed becomes:
questions.explanation: mv = (3m/4)V, so V = 4v/3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ball strikes a vertical wall at 10 m/s and rebounds horizontally at 10 m/s. Therefore:
options: acceleration occurs only if its initial direction was horizontal
the velocity changes, so acceleration occurs during collision
its momentum is unchanged even though it accelerates
questions.explanation: The ball reverses velocity, so its momentum changes and it accelerates during impact.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When two bodies stick together after a collision, it is:
questions.explanation: Sticking together is the defining case of a perfectly inelastic collision.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ball drops 10 m and stops after embedding 1 m into sand. Considering the full ball–sand–Earth system as closed, which is conserved?
options: total momentum, but not kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Total momentum of a closed system is conserved, while kinetic energy is dissipated into heat/deformation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Rocket propellant is expelled at 40 kg/s with exhaust speed 5 × 10⁴ m/s. The thrust is:
questions.explanation: Thrust = mass-flow rate × exhaust speed = 40 × 50,000 = 2×10⁶ N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Tripling a car's speed increases its stopping distance (under constant braking deceleration) by a factor of:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance d = v²/(2a), so tripling v makes d nine times larger.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A boy of mass m jumps onto a moving elastic board of mass M. If the board acquires momentum mv, its kinetic energy becomes:
questions.explanation: For board momentum p = mv, its kinetic energy is K = p²/(2M) = m²v²/(2M).
